story_text:
## The Illusion of Ownership (kind of sucks)
Modern-day tech has an ownership crisis. Locked-down devices, walled-garden ecosystems, legal-threats; it has never felt more like you are renting everything you buy despite being given a receipt for a product and not a rental service.
This ties into the core philosophy around the Vector Gear / Andromeda. We not only wanted VR options that have all the modern features we know and love, but also wanted the peace of mind of knowing that we own those devices and can fix, modify, and expand them in any way we wish. After many years of internal R&D by our Prominence team and a successful showcasing of our prototypes at Tokyo Game Show 2026, we want to take the next step and turn these prototypes into true polished headsets available to all of you. Once one is in your hands, it is yours to use and tinker with however you want; no artificial walls, locks, or roadblocks. Jailbroken by design, we cant wait to see some of the crazy things you come up with.
## Community Friendly
As we stated before, we wanted VR solutions that were open and free so that we could truly own what we have. To that end, we plan to make our custom hardware and software stacks either source-available or completely open source as we open up the ecosystem over time.
We will also be progressively preparing and releasing learning materials and documentation in waves that everyone can use as references to repair, modify, and expand their headset however they wish, with plans to sell the
We want to make sure that every tool in the shop is available to you, and these are just some of the ways we are working to make that happen.
## The Vector Gear: Our Flagship Standalone Option
The Chosen One. Packed with modern features and specs, yet fully open for you to tinker with (and hopefully not break).
## The Compute
At the core is a Qualcomm Snapdragon 8cx Gen 3 SoC with 8GB of LPDDR4 RAM tasked with handling all OS tasks (games, tools, XRUIOS, etc.). Paired with it is a dedicated RK3588 co-processor with its own dedicated 8GB of LPDDR4 RAM exclusively handling all tracking and other features such as foveated streaming. This split architecture ensures that accuracy stays sharp even through the worst of heavy workloads and lag-spikes, and also enables us to selectively choose what is active for both of our operation modes; Standalone Mode and Link Mode.
Under Standalone Mode, the full architecture is utilized to give you a traditional standalone experience. Under Link Mode, only the RK3588 is utilized, resulting in a traditional direct PCVR experience similar to what is offered by the Andromeda while maximizing battery life.
## The Displays
Painting the pictures are dual 2160x2160 TFT LCD 90hz panels. The headset itself has auto IPD adjustment, supporting a 58 to 70mm range.
## The Optics
For the Vector Gear, we experimented to see if we could reap some of the benefits of pancake lenses without having to pay the astronomically higher cost, and what we came up with are our custom dual-fresnels we have dubbed ‘Pseudo-Pancakes’.
Dual-fresnel headsets of old required a long distance between the eye and the panel, resulting in a narrow sweet spot and bulkier/heavier packages. A classic example is the well known Valve Index, which had an eye-to-panel distance of ~55mm. Utilizing our Pseudo-Pancakes, we have managed to achieve a distance of ~33mm for the Vector Gear, matching modern options like the Meta Quest 3! This allows us to have a large sweet spot in a modern compact package for a fraction of the cost of pancake lenses.
If you are curious and want to know more, you can view the project on hackaday.
## The Tracking/Cameras
The Vector utilizes full inside-out tracking, removing the need for any outside tracking equipment. Two interior eye-tracking cameras combined with a single interior mouth tracking camera are built into the headset, enabling full face and eye tracking. We also included two color passthrough cameras, ready for productivity tasks and experimenting with Mixed Reality.
## The Controllers
Our Vector controller is Steam Frame inspired with a similar form factor and button/stick layout, rumble support, and capacitive finger tracking. Under the hood lies a dedicated RK3576 paired with two cameras, allowing full inside-out tracking even when occluded (like with the Quest Pro). Two are included with your Vector Gear.
## The Storage/Expandability
For storage we have an internal 512GB NVME connected via M.2. Nothing is soldered, so you can easily upgrade or replace whenever you want, and if you need quick expansion we include a MicroSD slot for easy expandable storage when needed. Lastly, we feature a custom PCIe based cartridge slot for high performance storage/expansion in addition to exposed PCB pins for those who want to jack in and really get deep into modding.
## The Battery/Power
The Vector is powered by a high-capacity 85Wh silicon battery, which is rated to provide ~4 hours of uptime under Standalone Mode and ~6+ hours of runtime under Link Mode (PCVR). Charging is delivered through USB-C PD, allowing for a power delivery of up to 100w for maximum speed.
## The Connectivity
The Vector will feature full Wi-Fi 7 support via a Qualcomm QCNCM865, allowing for fast high-quality foveated PCVR streaming with little latency.
For those that have a shared Wi-Fi network or limited connectivity, some time after the campaign ends we will allocating some development towards our dedicated wireless dongle that offers a direct channel between your PC and your Vector, similar to the Steam Frame. This will be a separate accessory that will be available for purchase.
## The Audio
For input the Vector will feature a dual microphone array. For output we are still experimenting with options that are available and trying to narrow down what will work best for our use case. More details will be provided in future updates as we work to nail things down.
## Spec Recap
- Compute: Qualcomm Snapdragon 8cx Gen 3 (OS) + RK3588 (tracking, streaming, etc.)
- Memory: 16GB LPDDR4 RAM (8GB dedicated to Snapdragon and 8GB to RK3588)
- Displays: Dual 2160x2160 TFT LCD 90hz Panels
- Optics: In-House Developed Dual-Fresnel Pseudo-Pancake Lenses
- Tracking: Full Inside-Out and Face/Eye Tracking
- Cameras: 2x Interior Eye-Tracking, 1x Interior Mouth Tracking. 2x Color-Passthrough (Mixed Reality)
- Controllers: 2x Vector Controllers (Steam Frame Inspired Layout, Rumble and Capacitive Finger Tracking, Independent Inside-Out Tracking like the Quest Pro, RK3576 Powered)
- Storage: 512GB Internal NVME SSD Connected via M.2
- Expansion: MicroSD Card Slot, PCIe Interfacing Cartridge Slot
- Battery: 85Wh Silicon Battery (~4 Hours of Operation in Standalone Mode, ~6+ Hours of Operation in Link Mode), USB-C PD Charging (Power Delivery up to 100W)
- Connectivity: Qualcomm QCNCM865 (Wi-Fi 7), Wireless Dongle Accessory (Separate Purchase)
- Audio (Input): Dual Microphone Array
- Audio (Output): TBD
## The Andromeda: Our Traditional PCVR Option
The Prodigal Son. Same powerful inside-out and face/eye tracking in a slimmed down PCVR package.
## The Compute
Like the Vector, the Andromeda utilizes an RK3588 processor for handling tracking and other features such as foveated streaming.
## The Displays
Two options exist for the Andromeda: Dual 2160x2160 TFT LCD 90hz panels like the Vector, or dual 2560x2560 OLED panels (Native at 75hz, or 1920x1920 upscaled at 90hz similar to the Bigscreen Beyond 2).
Just like the Vector Gear, all Andromeda units also have auto IPD adjustment, supporting a 58 to 70mm range.
## The Optics
For the Andromeda LCD, the plan is to use our Pseudo-Pancake lenses same as the Vector. For the Andromeda OLED, we opted to use traditional pancake lenses to ensure the best possible fidelity with its OLED panels. We may consider a Pseudo-Pancake OLED option in the future depending on interest and how the campaign goes.
## The Tracking/Cameras
The same camera config as the Vector is used for full inside-out and face tracking, but with a slight exception where the mouth tracking camera is utilized as an attachment rather than built into the headset. One caveat is that the Andromeda does not include dual color-passthrough cameras, but this could always change based on interest and how the campaign goes.
## The Controllers
The Andromeda utilizes the same Vector controller as our standalone option, full inside out tracking even when occluded. Two are included here as well.
## The Battery/Power
The same high-capacity 85Wh silicon battery as the Vector, rated for ~6+ hours of uptime and featuring up to 100w charging via USB-C PD.
## The Connectivity
The Andromeda will utilize a Qualcomm QCNCM865 as well, so you can expect the same Wi-Fi 7 speed, reliability, and foveated streaming support that the Vector has. The Andromeda will also be fully supported by our wireless dongle once it is available for purchase same as the Vector.
## The Audio
For input the Andromeda will also feature a dual microphone array. For output we are still experimenting with options like with the Vector. Expect future updates as we work to nail this down as well.
## Spec Recap
- Compute: RK3588 (tracking, streaming, etc.)
- Memory: 8GB LPDDR4 RAM
- Displays: Dual 2160x2160 TFT LCD 90hz Panels (Andromeda LCD), Dual 2560x2560 OLED Panels (Andromeda OLED; Native at 75hz, or 1920x1920 upscaled at 90hz similar to the Bigscreen Beyond 2)
- Optics: In-House Developed Dual-Fresnel Pseudo-Pancake Lenses (Andromeda LCD), Traditional Pancake Lenses (Andromeda OLED)
- Tracking: Full Inside-Out and Face/Eye Tracking
- Cameras: 2x Interior Eye-Tracking, 1x Exterior Mouth Tracking (Attachment).
- Controllers: 2x Vector Controllers (Steam Frame Inspired Layout, Rumble and Capacitive Finger Tracking, Independent Inside-Out Tracking like the Quest Pro, RK3576 Powered)
- Battery: 85Wh Silicon Battery (~6+ Hours of Operation), USB-C PD Charging (Power Delivery up to 100W)
- Connectivity: Qualcomm QCNCM865 (Wi-Fi 7), Wireless Dongle Accessory (Separate Purchase)
- Audio (Input): Dual Microphone Array
- Audio (Output): TBD
## Our Software Stack, Developed In-House
## Shinra Meisin
Our face tracking framework, utilized by both the Vector and the Andromeda to power the face tracking pipeline. Shinra Meisin reads full gaze, pupil, eyelid, eyebrow, and mouth data from a headsets face-tracking camera array and translates everything to Unified Expressions OSC streams. Unified Expressions is an open-source standard for face and eye tracking which platforms like VRChat natively support, so you can be comfortable knowing that everything should work right out out box with limited setup.
As a part of development, we are making plans to host a paid 60+ person data collection event consisting of people from all nationalities. We will be using this data to harden Shinra Meisin to ensure accurate tracking for all eye shapes and skin tones. The event will be scheduled sometime after the campaign ends, so keep a lookout for updates if you want to know more.
## AstroSLAM
Our inside-out tracking implementation powering both the Vector and the Andromeda. It uses several state of the art techniques, such as an attention system that prioritizes distinct high-value features in the environment as anchors for SLAM calculations. This allows us to maintain high precision tracking while reducing both power draw and latency.
## YuukOS
Our custom arch-based OS built to power the Vector Gear, handling both the usual OS tasks and the management/communication of our split compute architecture. Both the FEX x86 emulation layer and the Proton compatibility layer are integrated by default, and we are exploring console emulation options as well with some discussion of a partnership with iiSU.
## The XRUIOS

risks: • This is our first attempt at bringing a physical product to market for mass distribution, and as expected we are not the most experienced in going through such a process. To help bridge the gap, we are working closely with our manufacturing partners to find the best ways forward. Should any hiccups occur, we plan to be fully transparent with everyone and update regularly to ensure that nobody is in the dark. • As the devices are still prototypes, we have not settled on the final hardware, designs, and form factors. We are still actively working on developing and polishing them further, and a portion of the funds from the campaign will be put towards getting towards a final prototype that we can push towards production. • The cost of components is constantly shifting and can spike at any time. To be able to offer the prices we have, we have gone through hundreds of manufacturers and tons of suppliers to find the best deals we can. Only when absolutely necessary will we raise any prices, and we will be fully transparent providing all the reasoning as to why. • Plastic injection molding takes a lot of time and money, and for a small team like ours we have to push for the most efficient use of both. For this reason we are looking to use soft alloy milled molds, which will have a much smaller upfront cost while lasting hundreds of runs. Once we have a finalized prototype, we will begin pivoting towards these molds for production. In the mean time prototypes will continue to utilize 3D printed shells to minimize costs. • Other companies such as Lynx and Decagear were not able to fully deliver on their promises despite having raised multitudes more funding than we are asking. To make sure we didn't make the same mistakes, we did our homework on where they failed (like trying to create a global supply chain for example). Instead of trying to own our entire manufacturing process, we decided to focus purely on development while entrusting parts manufacturing to experienced third-parties. From there the plan is to have them sent back to us and our partners for assembly, quality control, validation, and finally shipping.

updates.title: Update 5: The PsuedoPancakes, Why They Exist And How They Work
updates.text:
Many times have we heard "What are the PsuedoPancakes" and "They are no good for a VR headset". Some do not know why it's called this in the first place!
This update is short and to the point, talking all about the history of the PsuedoPancakes/why they were made, the math behind them and why work and finally a video demo of them actually working!

updates.text:
First off, HOLY COW PEOPLE!
Never did I expect we would hit over $33k in just 6 days! Thank you to everyone who's been part of making this all become a reality!
Moreover, I wanted to share some updates on a few general things!

I've recently been asked about the XRUIOS and how it works! Someone believed you had to replace your entire OS or couldn't use the XRUIOS with Steam. Both of these are false!
